text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: streaming path p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (SSE) > 12s, currently 13.7s. auto-escalation to oncall.

maya: seeing client reports of partial payloads + long tail, lots of 200s but final chunk delayed. p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 13s.

sam: thanks. is this isolated to one region or global? dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-latency?orgId=1

jordan: EU node spiking first, now US also creeping up. throughput steady, error rate low. looks like backpressure/queueing rather than CPU/OOM.

li: tcp connection counts are normal, but proxy write latency to clients shows a long tail. suspect proxy output queue build-up.

ops_oncall: i'm on it, joining call. quick mitigation: can we flip keepalive heartbeat to 15s -> 8s on the edge? might reveal slow consumers.

maya: good idea. @deploy-bot can we patch ALB/edge config short-term?

deploy-bot: triggered config change: edge.keepalive=8s for streaming-proxy (canary on prod-edge-3). rollout id: r-2024-11-23-01

nina-cs: customers flagged UX: spinner never finishes for ~10% of streaming requests, some report reconnects. tracking impacted accounts: acct-42, acct-77, acct-91. CS notified.

sam: digging into proxy logs, grep shows repeated `EPIPE` delays followed by eventual flushes. snippet:

```
2024-11-23T01:12:03Z proxy-3 write: queued 1024 bytes, client backpressure 4600ms
2024-11-23T01:12:15Z proxy-3 write: flush completed after 11000ms
```

jordan: that suggests the proxy's socket send buffer is stuck waiting for client. might be slow consumer causing per-connection drift and overall egress queue saturation.

li: two options: 1) proactively drop very slow consumers (kick threshold) to free pipeline, 2) enable per-connection write-bandwidth limit to avoid head-of-line blocking. runbook suggests kick after 8s stall for streaming routes.

ops_oncall: can we apply runbook step now? quick config patch: `streaming.proxy.slow_consumer_kick=8000ms` and enable `write_backpressure_limit=64KB`. roll can be done to all edges within ~3m.

maya: do it. prefer canary on prod-edge-1 then fast roll. add a log tag so we can revert easily.

deploy-bot: rolling slow_consumer_kick=8000ms to prod-edge-1 (canary). cfg-change-id: cfg-83421.

sam: monitoring: after canary, p99 on prod-edge-1 dropped from 13.7s -> 1.8s for that subset. global still elevated.

jordan: start full rollout. deploy-bot: please proceed.

deploy-bot: full rollout triggered, expected finish ~3m.

maria (ops_oncall): note — doing aggressive kick will drop some client connections; CS already queued messaging for affected accounts. recommend temporary message to customers: "We detected streaming connection problems and have applied a fix; please refresh if you see incomplete responses."

nina-cs: sent outbound note to impacted customers with temporary guidance.

sam: after full rollout, global p99 down to 2.1s, p95 steady ~1.1s. tail incidents reduced but we still see intermittent reappearance on one backend pool. digging into backend logs.

li: backend pool `streamer-az3` shows bursts of `chunk-serialize` stage pausing for GC around the same times, ~200ms pause but then a backlog causes longer flushes at proxy. investigating GC config and small object churn.

jordan: can we temporarily route traffic away from streamer-az3? easiest is to mark it draining in the router for 10m while we inspect.

ops_oncall: manual drain started for streamer-az3. routing weight -> 0 over 2m. watch for error spikes.

sam: once drained, p99 stabilized to 1.4s. looks like a problematic instance. we've opened a ticket to repro GC pauses locally.

li: probable root causes being layered: slow consumer client behavior causing proxy egress queueing + one backend instance with occasional long serialize/GC pauses amplifying tail. mitigation flow worked (kick + drain).

maya: follow-ups: - add automated detection to proactively throttle or kick persistent slow consumers (threshold + sampled metrics) - add per-instance streaming health check to avoid routing to serialize-pausing hosts - add end-to-end tracing from client chunk ack -> proxy write to identify slow clients quickly

ops_oncall: agreed. i've updated incident runbook and created an action item list in the incident ticket. ticket link: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/INF-4142

deploy-bot: note: config rollback available r-2024-11-23-01 (edge.keepalive) and cfg-83421 (slow_consumer_kick) with one-click revert.

nina-cs: customers acknowledge the messaging, two asked for timeline for permanent fix. I'll coordinate with PM/Eng to get ETA.

sam: next steps for engineering: reproduce GC pause, add metrics for `proxy.egress_queue_ms` per-host, instrument client ack path. I'll own the first 2.

li: i'll own the runbook items and the streaming health probe rollout.

maya: thanks all. summary for postmortem: immediate triage: applied slow_consumer_kick + keepalive change -> reduced p99 from 13.7s to ~1.4s, drained flawed backend -> stabilized. Customer impact: partial response delays for ~8-12% of streaming requests for affected accounts during the spike window (~01:10-01:35 UTC). Owners and next steps tracked in INF-4142.

incident-bot: Incident declared SEV2. Link to triage doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/INF-4142/triage-notes

maya: marking this thread resolved for live mitigation. please add any additional observations in INF-4142 before EOD. :white_check_mark:
